environment.machine: Windows 10, 8 logical CPU laptop (shared with negev_express + supabase docker stacks)
environment.backend: Node 22, Express, single instance, PG_POOL_MAX=30, NODE_ENV=production, RL_MAX=1000000 (limiter effectively off for single-IP generator)
environment.db: postgres:18 docker (wasaly-lt-pg:5455) shared_buffers=512MB, pg_stat_statements on, SSL on
environment.redis: redis:7 docker (wasaly-lt-redis:6399), socket.io redis adapter enabled
environment.note: Laptop + co-tenant containers => absolute numbers are a FLOOR; Railway dedicated resources will be higher.

breaking_point.observation: throughput plateaus ~115 rps beyond 50 VUs; extra VUs only add queueing latency; 0 errors throughout (graceful)

bottleneck.primary: PostgreSQL CPU (saturated ~700% of 8 cores under load; avg 431% during soak)
bottleneck.secondary: pg pool saturated at 30 active conns; Node is I/O-bound (RAM ~180MB, low CPU)

socket_capacity.note: fast handshake bursts (>300/s) caused transient websocket errors because each handshake does a DB auth SELECT; gentle ramp reached 3000/3000 clean

prod_probe.aborted: yes - safety abort at ~36s when err>2%
prod_probe.failures_cause: HTTP 429 from prod per-IP limiter (300 req/min); 35 rps = 2100/min from one IP. NOT server errors.

scaling_factor.method: prod p95 minus ~212ms network RTT = prod server time; vs local
scaling_factor.note: Prod server-side latency (~60-90ms) comparable-to-better than laptop local; Railway DB is faster than co-tenant laptop pg. Capacity below is derived from laptop floor and scaled conservatively.
